reviews.text: I really appreciate how the doctor explained everything in detail. 😁 I'll continue coming to the hospital! …

■Incidents
Incorrect prescription (unwilling to admit)
Miscommunication regarding drug interactions (admitted)
While waiting in the waiting room, witnessed the staff handing out medication packets intended for another animal.

■Suspicious Points
The level of detail in the medical record varies among staff members ← Sometimes the current situation is discussed based on information from before the examination results from a month ago.

There is absolutely no mention of the contents of the medications administered.

← Is it acceptable for a hospital to not include this information unless requested? While it may not be legally problematic since it involves animals, what about the hospital's literacy?

The workload may be immense, but there are many sloppy aspects.

My Java sparrow couldn't climb its perch and wouldn't eat or drink for the first day. It just huddled there with its eyes closed, and I braced myself for its end. But on the second day, it reacted slightly to the family and tried to move, so I called for advice.

Fortunately, they were able to see a doctor, and it was admitted for IV fluids and an X-ray. The next day, after receiving explanations and realizing its condition was critical, it was discharged.

After returning home, we were able to spend a few hours together as a family, its final moments.

Thank you for everything during this short time.

Thank you very much.

Has that brown-haired nurse left?

I used to go to the clinic regularly, but that nurse was harsh with a new staff member in front of other patients, and even when I was paying, she would push her work onto someone else, laughing loudly in the background saying things like "This is so cute!" which was very unpleasant.

My pet bird passed away, so I haven't been there for a while, but I'm planning to get another parakeet soon, and the doctors are all very nice, so I want to go for a check-up, but I'm worried that if that nurse is there again, I'll get irritated.

Before the clinic moved, there was a receptionist/nurse with a bad attitude, but since then everyone who has helped me has been very nice. The thought of that nurse being at reception or somewhere similar again is unbearable. On the other hand, there was someone I thought was very helpful; I wonder if they've left? If so, I think they should reconsider who they keep and who they let go.

This happened a while ago, but I was considering going back for another check-up, so I wrote this hoping for improvements. I hope this catches the director's eye.
I always appreciate the thorough examinations I receive!
I have a veterinarian I've been going to for checkups and nail trims for a long time. They give me appropriate advice, and as a pet owner, they are a great help.
They were very kind. There are hardly any hospitals specializing in birds, so I'm grateful that they examined my Java sparrow so carefully.

My 4-year-old female parakeet
She was unable to lay her first egg successfully.
I had been taking her to a local veterinary hospital that treats small birds, but their treatment plan (waiting until the egg mummified) left me feeling utterly devastated.

Considering the limited time she had left to live, with the egg turning red and popping out in pain with every strain, I felt I had no choice but to entrust my hopes to a specialist in small birds. I searched online and made an appointment.

The receptionist was kind and polite, and the doctor who examined her was truly wonderful. He explained the situation carefully, performed the treatment quickly, and gave advice on her future care.

I am deeply grateful to this hospital for treating her and saving her life.

The other patients who came in at the same time also showed the trust placed in this hospital.

Thank you to all the staff for your compassionate examination and care.

I felt this was a specialized bird hospital where I could consult with them about the appropriate treatment plan depending on the situation.

The treatment details from each veterinarian are ultimately shared with the hospital director, and the hospital proposes the best treatment plan for both the animal and the owner.

I received treatment for my greater sulfur crested cockatoo there.

However, if you're driving from outside Tokyo, finding parking is unavoidable. Parking in Tokyo is expensive. 😓

I've been having my bird checked by the head veterinarian every six months for nine years now. I sometimes leave my bird at their hotel when I travel. It's considerably more expensive than pet shop hotels, but I feel safe because it's a hospital. My bird will be getting old in a few years, so I expect to rely on them even more, but I trust them completely.

I was shocked by the young woman at the reception desk's complete lack of knowledge!
When I asked about the system, she said, "I'll check."
When I told her I wanted to see the head veterinarian, who presumably sees many birds, she said, "There's a nomination fee." "How much is it?" "I'll check." "5500 yen." "Is it every time?" "I'll check."
Is this really okay? This person is at the reception desk...
I was shocked by the nomination fee, which is on par with a high-class hostess club.
I visited because it seemed like they had a good reputation after opening this clinic from Yokohama Bird Hospital, but
both the receptionist and the doctor who examined me lacked knowledge. I was simply astonished that they could even make a living like this! I was just utterly shocked.

My Java Sparrow, who had a hernia, injured his right leg and visited us for the first time. There didn't appear to be any fractures, but I was asked if I wanted an X-ray just to be sure. That was a complete mistake. When my dog ​​returned from the X-ray, even his left leg, which had been perfectly normal, was bent in an odd position. I wonder how much pressure they must have put on his protruding abdomen due to the hernia to get the X-ray. When I took him home and looked at him, he was clearly bleeding from his internal organs, and he looked much weaker than before we went to the hospital. Even when I told them that something was wrong with his left leg, they simply said, "Maybe it's because he was sitting down." I was a fool to believe them. I nursed him desperately, but he passed away the next morning alone. I can't forgive myself for bringing him to this hospital and causing him such pain in his final moments, even though he only had a leg injury. The director is apparently well-known, but perhaps I was unlucky to have been treated by a young doctor. After he passed away, I took him to see his doctor on the Shinkansen, but there was still internal bleeding. I want my lost dog back.
We moved from Morishita to Asakusabashi and are now spacious, which is a relief.
Morishita Kotori's hospital is the best!!

The vet was inexplicably irritable and confrontational throughout the entire visit. Their handling of the bird was also very rough and careless, so I cannot confidently entrust my pet to this hospital.

The reception and phone service were also terrible. It's sad to think that if there were more specialized bird hospitals, I wouldn't need to go to a place like this.

On Monday, he was admitted to the hospital for a new consultation. I visited him every day, but he lost weight day by day, and on Thursday afternoon, I received a call saying that I could pick him up. Given his condition, I offered to pick him up immediately, but they flatly refused, saying they were fully booked and that I would need to make an appointment to visit him. On my way to the hospital, I received a call informing me that he had passed away... I regret not having tried to pick him up on Wednesday. I'm sure there were various reasons on the hospital's side, but I cannot accept this response. I wanted to be there for him in his final moments... That's the kind of attitude this hospital has.
They take a very good look at your condition and the waiting time is short.

It's difficult to find a hospital specializing in small birds, so I searched diligently and finally found this one.

My lovebird suddenly became ill, and I'm grateful that the doctors were able to see it as soon as possible despite how busy they were. Since then, I've been bringing my bird in for health checkups approximately every six months. I think it's a wonderful hospital where everything is done with great care and kindness.
There are very few hospitals that can treat birds. This one has a very nice environment, and the doctor explained the bird's condition very clearly.

I always use your nail trimming service.

There's a parking meter right in front of the shop, so if you're lucky, parking will cost around 300 yen for 60 minutes.

This was my first time using your services. There are few hospitals with specialized knowledge of birds, so it's understandable that it's always crowded, but the only way to contact them as a new patient is by phone, and it's always busy. I finally got through and made an appointment, but something came up and I wanted to change the date and time, but it was always busy no matter how many times I called before the day of the appointment. In that case, I was told to leave a message on the answering machine, but it was always busy so it didn't go to voicemail, and even though I couldn't get through at all, it was treated as a same-day cancellation and I was charged a cancellation fee. I hope this will be improved as well. The doctor's diagnosis was thorough and good, and I appreciate that there is an inquiry form for subsequent visits, but I think the handling of new patients needs improvement.

It's been a while since I've been here, but I'm glad it's now easier to access than the previous location. There is a parking meter on the street in front, so you can park on the side of the road for up to an hour.

I've never written a review before, but this hospital is so excellent that I wanted to share it with other parakeet owners.

I used to go to another hospital, but it wasn't a bird specialist, and they gave me vague advice, so I wanted to switch to a bird specialist hospital and chose Morishita Bird Hospital.

If you make a reservation, there's almost no waiting time, and you'll be seen right on time.

The examination is very thorough, and the doctor is kind and answers all your questions.

My worries about my parakeet have decreased, and I feel much more at ease.

I highly recommend this hospital.

This was my second time calling the bird hospital, which requires phone reservations. I was turned down again. The receptionist had no available spots on the waiting list, so after calling in the morning, they called again in the evening, but they didn't see me the first time, so I had to take my parakeet to the hospital.
*2024

This time (for the first time in a year and a half), I also called to make a reservation because another parakeet was sick, but they told me they were on the waiting list and it was over.
They instructed me to ask for the name over the phone, but...I said just in case...and they never called.
Looks like it's not meant to be.

*August 2025
They were very kind and helpful.

I had previously visited two other hospitals, but both only provided a consultation and observation without detailed examinations or explanations, and simply prescribed medication, which left me feeling somewhat distrustful.
However, this time, my first visit to this hospital resulted in thorough examinations and careful explanations, and I was extremely satisfied.
The examination was conducted with great care, and I could feel the doctor's love for birds.
The cost is higher compared to the previous hospitals, but I consider it to be the price for the explanations and peace of mind 😊
Even though it's a bit far, I would want to make this my regular vet because I felt so at ease.

The doctor who looked after my Java sparrow was very kind and patient with me during the examination. The cashier was also kind and polite! 
Unfortunately, my Java sparrow passed away at the age of 10, but I would like to use his services again if I ever need to raise another small bird.

I'm a huge fan of Dr. Yorizaki.

I look forward to my semi-annual check-ups! The waiting room is full of bird lovers, so it's always a very relaxing space with lots of bird talk and information exchange.

Thanks to Dr. Yorizaki, my female budgie has been free of illness and hasn't laid an egg since her initial check-up where she was treated for megabacteria. The first photo is from when she was young, and the second is from when she's 10 years old.

I'm so grateful for the detailed instructions on how to care for her (including how to prevent her from going into heat). Currently, I'm discussing preparing for her old age, or rather, creating a gentle environment for her, at each check-up.

Even after moving from Tokyo, I was hesitant to find a new bird specialist hospital (the more I read reviews of other hospitals), so I continue to have regular check-ups at this hospital, even though it's far away. Another pet owner I happened to speak with, who had traveled a similar distance as me, shared the same opinion. She's a very trustworthy and kind female veterinarian.

As a side note, the waiting room has a clear list of consultation fees displayed below the reception counter, and the costs for examinations and treatments are confirmed verbally – the pricing is very transparent. I wrote this because I was confused after reading other reviews. If you're feeling anxious about your first visit, I think having the head veterinarian examine your pet will alleviate your concerns.

For a pet owner, nothing is more important than having a healthy and happy pet. We'll continue to rely on their services!

I've been taking my budgie to this clinic. Even with an appointment, there's sometimes a bit of a wait (it's a veterinary clinic, after all; I think it's the same for humans), but if you let them know the situation in advance via their web form, they understand and respond flexibly.

This is one of only a few bird-specialized hospitals in Tokyo.

Therefore, it's crowded on weekdays as well as weekends, but the doctors are incredibly thorough in their examinations, for which I am extremely grateful.

When I recently visited, I was told that they couldn't accept a walk-in first-time patient, so I recommend visiting regularly for health checkups to manage your bird's health.

As many others have written, you should start by learning how to serve people at the reception desk. 
We'll talk about it after that. 
Many people probably use this hospital out of necessity, but there are plenty of better hospitals in Tokyo that treat birds.

For the past year or so, I've been visiting the hospital several times a month for my pet bird's illness.
It's true that it's difficult to get through on the phone, but they always …

I've always received treatment here.
My cockatiel had some trouble with one of his legs, so I went to make an appointment on January 20th. …
The receptionist's tone on the phone was harsh, and I found the conversation unpleasant. …
The website said it was by appointment only, so I called, but I couldn't get through. …
I recently started keeping budgies, and after reading that they often carry infections like megabacteria, I took my budgie in for its first health checkup. …
